newsitem.title: GERMANY: German asylum home blaze kills one, hurts 40 - radio.
newsitem.headline: German asylum home blaze kills one, hurts 40 - radio.

text.p: German radio on Wednesday said one person had died and 40 people were injured in a blaze in a home for asylum seekers in the southern town of Friedrichshafen.
The radio said police were not ruling out the possibility of arson and many people had been injured in the chaos of trying to escape from the building.
Police were not immediately available for independent confirmation of the blaze.
Just over a a week ago, suspected right-wing extremists set fire to a church in the eastern town of Luebeck, prompting politicians and religious leaders to call for a clampdown on extremists.

Suspected neo-Nazis daubed swastikas on the facade of St Vicelin Church and set a fire which spread to the church. They also scrawled the name of a local priest whose parish is sheltering a family of asylum seekers to prevent their deportation to Algeria.

The attack, which gutted the Roman Catholic church, sparked fears that record post-war unemployment was sparking a new wave of racist violence like that seen after German unification when asylum-seekers' hostels often became targets of arson attacks.
